_readme: Manually-verified frame placements for the thumbnails in this directory, to score boundaries::detect against instead of eyeballing annotated TIFFs. `frames` is each frame's start column; the frame is `length` columns wide, where length = format.height_dots(dpi) and dpi comes off the TIFF's own XResolution tag - neither is duplicated here so a re-scan at a different resolution doesn't go stale. Edit this with `scripts/annotate.py`, not by hand. Frame starts here come from examples/column_profile.rs's texture/density read, independent of detect()'s own dpi handling; `length` for scoring should still come from the TIFF's own XResolution tag at test time, read as RATIONAL (see examples/detect_frames.rs's `resolution()`), not assumed. Two files (*_overlapping_*) draw real frames that overlap on the film itself, so their entries keep detect()'s own columns as a lower-confidence reference rather than a fabricated split.

35mm_color_neg_full_roll.tiff.note: a whole roll fed through in one pass: 6104 columns, film to 5449 and holder past that. The wind is regular, so these are a least-squares ladder (pitch 143.246, first frame at 0.29) fitted over the frames the profile places unambiguously and then extended across the whole film span - residuals under 8 columns everywhere. Frames 1-4 are the leader end: 1 and 4 are unexposed base, 2 and 3 are thin but real. They are on the film and on the wind, so they count

35mm_color_neg_mising_frames.tiff.note: detect() reports 5 heavily-overlapping frames tiled across columns 6-560; the profile shows real content only at the ends of that span (6-130 and 430-570), flat unexposed base in between (density matches the confirmed gaps elsewhere in the file) - this strip has one frame's worth of film never exposed, not five real frames

6x6_bw_3frames.tiff.note: frame 1 was placed at 120 here, at the first real texture. That is not its edge: the film's flat runs are 44-128, 239-267, 452-466 and 651-661, and 56/262/468 are the only columns that put a whole 183-wide frame between one flat run and the next. Frame 1 simply carries no exposure over its first 70 columns

6x6_bw_3frames_dense.tiff.note: frame 1 was placed at 40, which is holder: the film starts at 44 and its first flat run is 44-56. Frames run gap to gap from 60, 243-261 and 660-669 being the flat runs that bracket them

6x6_color_neg_overlapping_3frames.tiff.note: overlapping by design (real under-advanced winding) - no clean gap to place a boundary against, kept detect()'s own columns as reference

6x9_color_neg_overlapping_2frames.tiff.note: overlapping by design (real under-advanced winding) - no clean gap to place a boundary against, kept detect()'s own columns as reference

holga_bw_2frames.tiff.note: frame 2 was placed at 260, past the flat run at 215-268. 238 is the reading the film supports: it puts frame 2's far edge at 421, against the flat run at 422-435, and the two frames really do share 7 columns - this is a Holga, whose 6x6 mask is narrower than its wind
